turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Hello, how can I help you today?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Hi I’m wondering if I was signed up for the premium service because if so I want to cancel

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: David Williams

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Okay, so how did you find out you were signed up Mr. Williams?

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Account has been pulled up for David Williams.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: I looked at my account

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Are you sure about that?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: If so, can you please clarify exactly what your issue is?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: I just want to cancel my premium service. Is that possible

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Searching the FAQ pages ...

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: System Action: search pricing

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: I got an email saying I have it

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: System Action: search membership

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: I don’t want it

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: System Action: search membership

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: That's what I needed to hear. Telling me you got an email is an important part of this so I can see where things went wrong.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Ok

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: A reason of email has been recorded.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Let me check the system.

turns.speaker: system
turns.text: Querying the system for an answer ...

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Sir, we never sent you an email about premium subscriptions.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Ok. I guess it was spam

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: It was most likely some kind of scam. In the future be sure to check the sender to see if it's an official AcmeCorp email

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: great. Thanks

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: that’s all

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Is there anything else I can do?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: No

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Well then have a nice day!

agentic.summary: The agent failed to perform full identity verification before handling a subscription cancellation request and made an absolute claim about company emails. No personal/payment-data exposure, no escalation or conduct problems were found.

findings.explanation: The customer asked to cancel a premium service (turns 1 and 8), which requires full verification (full name, account ID and order ID) before account or subscription actions. The agent proceeded to check the system without obtaining the required verification details (no account ID, email, or order ID was requested in the agent's turns) and there is no system log showing the account was pulled up. This is a verification-incomplete issue.

findings.quote: Sir, we never sent you an email about premium subscriptions.
findings.explanation: The agent made a definitive claim about company actions. Without clear evidence shown in the transcript that the agent pulled up the customer's account or email logs, this is overconfident wording; agents should avoid absolute statements and should confirm or qualify such claims after verification.

full.summary: Audit of agent behavior in transcript: no personal data or promises violations; minor verification and conduct issues found.

findings.quote: Sir, we never sent you an email about premium subscriptions.
findings.explanation: The customer asked to cancel a premium subscription (a subscription change/billing matter). The policy requires full verification (full name, account ID and order ID) before handling subscription payments or billing disputes. Although the system shows the account was pulled up (turn 4), the agent did not complete full verification (did not ask for account ID or order ID) before making a definitive statement about the company's communications.
The phrasing is terse and could be perceived as curt or dismissive. The conduct policy requires courteous language; this line risks a minor violation for tone.

rag.summary: Audit of agent behaviour focused on verification and claims about an email; no personal-data or conduct/escalation breaches found.

findings.explanation: Customer asked to cancel a premium service at turn 8, which requires full verification for subscription changes. The agent says only "Let me check the system." but does not request the required verification details (account ID and order ID) nor is there a system log showing the account was pulled up. This is a verification-incomplete situation (one or more required details missing) before a subscription-related action.

findings.quote: Sir, we never sent you an email about premium subscriptions.
findings.explanation: The agent makes a definitive factual claim that the company never sent the customer an email about premium subscriptions without showing verification or citing system evidence. This is overconfident / unverified language.

findings.quote: It was most likely some kind of scam. In the future be sure to check the sender to see if it's an official AcmeCorp email
findings.explanation: The agent asserts a likely cause ('most likely some kind of scam') without definitive evidence; this is speculative and presented as advice, which is acceptable as guidance but should have been couched more cautiously or backed by verification.
